topic: Slope-Intercept and Intercept Forms of a Line
title: Where Does It Cross? Intercepts Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
A town has two main streets crossing at the centre, and a new straight road cuts across both. Can the road's equation tell us both crossing points at a glance? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 9, Straight Lines) we learn the slope-intercept form y = mx + c and the intercept form x/a + y/b = 1.

You will watch a line slide up as c counts from -2 to 2 while its slope stays fixed, then turn around its y-crossing as m changes. We derive y = mx + c from the point-slope form, build x/a + y/b = 1 from the two crossings, compare the two forms side by side, learn to get y alone before reading m and c, and rewrite 3x + 2y = 12 in both forms. Two pause-and-think questions, the exam trap of reading intercepts when the right side is not 1, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
